_note: Industry, street, ownership, moat, critiques and gaps for the Q1FY27 initiation. Only sources published on or before 30-Sep-2026; later facts go to updates/later-facts.json.

fertiliser.point: Indian fertiliser consumption (POS) 71.0 mt in FY26 (62.9 mt FY23): urea 39.7, DAP 9.4, NPK 14.1, SSP 5.5, MOP 2.3. Production 50.9 mt; imports 23.1 mt (16.0 mt in FY25).
NPKs are now ~60% of phosphatic fertilisers; DAP+NPK consumption ~24 mt; domestic phosphatic production 16 mt and imports 10 mt in FY26 (7 mt in FY25).

India imports >80% of its ammonia and sulphur, mostly through the Strait of Hormuz; the Middle East crisis lifted ammonia to ~$840-850/t and sulphur to ~$800/t (May-2026); phosphoric acid contract $1,290 → $1,360 (Q1FY27) → $1,700/t (Q2FY27).
Q1FY27 industry: DAP+NPK production -21% and imports -38% as low NBS rates made NP/NPK unviable; consumption flat; channel stocks comfortable for kharif.
NBS Kharif 2026 (Apr-Sep): ₹41,534 cr, ~10% higher per-kg rates for N, P and S; rabi 2026-27 rates not announced by 30-Sep-2026. FY27 budget: ₹1.17 lakh cr urea, ₹54,000 cr NBS (Feb-2026).

2026 south-west monsoon: 87% of the long-period average (June 65%, July 101%, Aug 84%, Sep 92%); south peninsula 76%, east & north-east 74%. Southern reservoirs were 28% full vs 65% a year earlier in July.

Policy: national urea investment policy (9-10 mt new capacity over 8 years); ₹37,500 cr coal/lignite gasification scheme; QR-code fertiliser sales traceability pilot in 10-12 states; reasonable-margin guidelines on P&K fertilisers pending clarity; nano fertilisers restricted in UP and Maharashtra.

cropProtection.point: Global channel destocking ended in FY26; Indian demand recovered in kharif 2025 but rabi was muted by the late monsoon withdrawal; kharif 2026 domestic demand muted by delayed sowing, exports improving.
China keeps active-ingredient prices low and intermediates high; Coromandel's key molecules (mancozeb etc.) are not ones China competes in, and it passed on cost increases in exports.

brokers.thesis: Crop protection the bright spot (standalone EBIT +44%); fertiliser margins hit by Middle East-led input inflation; FY27E cut 10%, FY28E maintained; FY26-28 EBITDA CAGR 18%, PAT 21%
Long-term story intact (crop protection, NACL); cut FY27-28 EPS on fertiliser margin pressure, rupee depreciation and lower subsidy support

older.method: 30x Q2FY28E EPS; ~15% revenue CAGR, CP to ~₹10,000 cr in five years

moat.dimension: Scale and distribution in South India
moat.evidence: Largest private phosphatic player: 17.5% consumption share, 4.3 mt DAP+NPK sales, ~1,200 own stores (76% profitable), 12,000 channel partners.
Own sulphuric and phosphoric acid (60% of needs from FY27), Senegal rock (71.5%), TIFERT and Foskor ties; kept producing in Q1FY27 when peers cut output.
MRP and subsidy set by government policy; Q1FY27 margins fell when NBS lagged costs; reasonable-margin guidelines cap returns.
35% of volumes from unique grades; SSP premium grades >50%; specialty nutrients at ~20% margin, but most NPK grades are commodities.
Strong in mancozeb and a few molecules; ~19% standalone margin; NACL at 11%; no proprietary molecules, CDMO only at launch-plant stage.
Net cash ~₹2,600 cr incl. ICDs (Mar-2026); AAA ratings; can carry subsidy receivables of ₹2,000-3,800 cr.
Manufactured EBITDA ~₹5,000/t (FY26), <₹3,500/t in Q4FY26; integration should help, but imported ammonia and sulphur remain the swing cost.

critiques.argument: Subsidy (NBS) rates lag raw-material costs: Kharif 2026 rates rose only ~10% while acid rose 25%+, and rabi rates were still pending at 30-Sep.
Depreciation and finance cost have stepped up (Q1FY27 D&A ₹203 cr vs ₹121 cr) so EBITDA growth converts poorly into EPS.
critiques.who: Analysts on the Q1FY27 call (Antique), GAM

critiques.argument: A weak 2026 monsoon in the south peninsula (76% of normal) and low reservoirs threaten rabi volumes in Coromandel's core markets.
NACL margins have plateaued at ~11% EBITDA; further improvement needs new products over 2-3 years; minority shareholders take 46%.
Working capital rises with input prices (subsidy outstanding ₹3,254 cr at Jun-2026), absorbing cash.
Crop protection and backward integration justify a re-rating to an 'agri-solutions' multiple of 25-30x.

gaps: Segment depreciation by quarter is not disclosed: quarterly segment margins are shown at PBIT level only.
Q1FY25 segment figures are derived (H1FY25 less Q2FY25).
Costs of the granulation, T-MAP, fluorination and mancozeb projects are not disclosed individually; FY27 capex is our estimate from capital commitments.
No disclosure of manufactured vs traded EBITDA, or of retail, specialty nutrient, nano and BMCC profits.
DAM Capital's valuation method and estimates were not available; only an aggregator summary of the note.
Rabi 2026-27 NBS rates were not known at the as-of date; our FY27 H2 margins are assumptions.
The ~10% share-price fall on 28-30 Sep 2026 (peers -1% to -4%) has no company announcement that explains it in the sources we found.
The minorities' future share of profit (NACL 46%, BMCC 28.5%, Dhaksha) is our assumption (₹0-20 cr a year).
Kharif 2026 per-kg NBS rates come from a secondary source, consistent with management's '10% increase'.
